answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a unique ceramic token from umber clay harvested only in a verified remote tundra region. A licensed artisan stamps a serial and GPS-tagged photo of the raw material, then a public ledger accepts one active key per serial. Extra identities demand extra clay shipments, each costing C in extraction, transport, and inspection. With per-identity reward capped at R, n sybils earn n(R-C), so cloning is profitable only if R exceeds the full tundra-to-forge chain cost; collusion on clay sources remains the residual risk.
